title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
measurement_description: The paper measured multiple aspects related to religion, including: 1) Performance disparities in toxicity detection for online comments that mention different religious groups (Christians, Muslims, other religions) using the CivilComments dataset. 2) The ability of language models to generate divisive social media posts targeting specific religious groups (Christians, Jews, Muslims) as part of a disinformation evaluation. 3) Social biases related to religion as one of nine demographic categories within the BBQ (Bias Benchmark for Question Answering) dataset.
findings: Key findings related to religion include: 1) In toxicity detection on the CivilComments dataset, almost all models were 'considerably more accurate and robust for comments mentioning Christians as compared to comments mentioning Muslims.' 2) For the disinformation 'wedging' task, models were prompted to generate divisive messages targeting religious groups (Christians, Jews, and Muslims), but the evaluation found that targeting specific audiences remains a challenge for the models. 3) The BOLD dataset was used to measure toxicity in generated text from prompts mentioning religious identities, among other categories.
